learn.title: CapEx, OpEx, consumption and pricing models
objectives: Tell capital expenditure (CapEx) apart from operational expenditure (OpEx).
Explain the consumption-based model and why it removes upfront cost.
Compare pay-as-you-go, reservations, savings plans and Spot pricing.
Recognise licensing options such as Azure Hybrid Benefit and the Azure free account.
concepts: CapEx
Upfront spending on physical assets such as servers and buildings. The cost is spread (depreciated) over the asset's life.
OpEx
Ongoing spending on services as you use them, such as a monthly cloud bill.
Consumption-based model
No upfront cost. Pay for what you use, and stop paying when you stop using it.
Pay-as-you-go
Default Azure pricing: no commitment, billed for actual usage, most flexible.
Azure Reservations
A one- or three-year commitment to a specific resource type in a chosen scope, for a large discount on steady workloads.
Azure savings plan for compute
A one- or three-year commitment to a fixed hourly spend that applies automatically across eligible compute services, sizes and regions.
Azure Spot Virtual Machines
Unused Azure capacity at a deep discount. Azure can evict them, so use them only for interruptible work.
Azure Hybrid Benefit
Use existing Windows Server or SQL Server licences (with Software Assurance or qualifying subscriptions) to cut Azure costs.
Azure free account
A credit for the first 30 days, 12 months of popular free services, and services that are always free within limits.
Serverless pricing
Pay per execution and the resources used while code runs; little or no cost when idle.
comparisons: Reservation: a specific resource type, biggest discount, least flexible. Savings plan: an hourly spend commitment, flexible across sizes, regions and services.
Pay-as-you-go suits unpredictable or short-lived workloads. Commitments suit steady, long-running ones.
Spot is cheapest but can be evicted with no SLA. Pay-as-you-go isn't evicted.
CapEx is paid up front and depreciated. OpEx is paid as consumed.
traps: A reservation is a billing discount. It doesn't create, reserve or start a VM.
Spot VMs have no availability SLA and can be evicted at any time.
Stopping a VM without deallocating it can keep compute charges running.
Azure Hybrid Benefit needs eligible existing licences. It isn't a free licence.
Consumption pricing means a variable bill, not a fixed one.
revision: Steady 24/7 on one VM type: reservation.
Steady compute spend that keeps changing size, region or service: savings plan.
Already own Windows Server or SQL Server licences: Azure Hybrid Benefit.
